channel.title: Thoughts by Your Hommie
channel.description: Statistical and machine learning cases, simulations that verify beliefs before the data arrives, and stats textbooks rewritten simpler.

item.title: Separation makes logistic regression fail loudly in the warnings and quietly in the estimates
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: As a predictor gets closer to perfectly separating a binary outcome, the maximum likelihood estimate diverges. R warns about fitted probabilities, not about the coefficient — which is the number people actually report.

item.title: A Normal(0, 10) prior on a logistic coefficient is not weak — it is a confident bet on certainty
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: Priors are chosen on the log-odds scale and interpreted as vague. Pushed through the inverse logit, a wide Normal prior puts most of its mass on probabilities of essentially 0 or essentially 1.

item.title: The standard error, rewritten without the sampling-distribution detour
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: Most textbooks introduce the standard error by first constructing an imaginary population of repeated samples. That detour is where readers lose the thread, and it is avoidable.
